method: Bounded comparison of PDFium source renders and native UTF-8 extraction: ten explicitly listed pages of 52. Same-assistant acquisition triage, not complete content review or independent authentication.

files.notes: Indictment with court filing header, highlighted printed allegations and handwritten final-page annotations. Native sampled prose broadly tracks source; handwriting and stamps on page 20 are noisy/omitted and need bounded source-assisted OCR assessment. Allegations are not findings of guilt. Only pages 1, 10 and 20 inspected; no full-content review or date adjudication.

Two-page nested email chain with redacted participants and seven detected header occurrences. Header continuations and body cross the page boundary; some recipient fragments occur after subject/body labels in native reading order. Attachment filenames do not establish separately acquired attachment contents. Preserve redactions; candidate/header/body review and date adjudication remain pending; no unique-message/contact claims.

Court conference transcript. Printed line numbers and captions are flattened ahead of prose in native extraction, and some words are imperfect; sampled substantive prose broadly tracks source. Three-page scope (1,14,28), not complete transcript review. Attribute statements to speakers; no identity, liability or primary-date inference from mentions.

Single sparse printed observation note; substantive text is present despite large blank area. Date range describes an observation interval, not an established document creation/issue day. No person identity, diagnosis or independent verification inferred. Date review pending.

Calendar event export with distinct scheduled start/end, created, modified and DTSTAMP fields, redacted organizer/attendees and Teams boilerplate. Not evidence of actual attendance or a person-to-person sent email. No participant identities or single primary date assigned. Native text broadly tracks visible nonredacted fields; parser detects zero email occurrences.
